items.headline: Jim Cramer picks Meta and Microsoft as top AI stocks
items.summary: Jim Cramer identified Meta as a preferred established-company exposure to the AI investment cycle, citing confidence that its management can monetize AI spending through products including Muse.

items.headline: Jim Cramer picks Meta and Microsoft as top AI stocks
items.summary: Jim Cramer favored Microsoft among established AI companies, emphasizing confidence in its leadership and potential to discover additional applications for the technology.

items.headline: Marvell Finds $400B AI Opportunity, But Shares Take a Hit
items.summary: Marvell's investor-day framework expanded its stated 2030 total addressable market to about $400 billion, including approximately $385 billion in data-center opportunities, while the stock declined in early trading after the event.

items.headline: Marvell Technology Targets Up to $90B Revenue by 2031 as AI Demand Accelerates
items.summary: Marvell outlined a path to $70 billion-$90 billion in annual fiscal 2031 revenue and raised its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to approximately $20 billion, attributing the expansion to AI infrastructure demand.

items.headline: Jim Cramer sees more AI upside ahead for Meta, Microsoft and AMD despite bubble fears
items.summary: Cramer said major technology companies including AMD could continue benefiting from AI adoption, while acknowledging concerns about high valuations and comparisons with the dot-com bubble.
